top_stories.title: New Attack Methods Enable Malware to Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
top_stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks researchers have demonstrated new attack methods that allow malware to hijack accounts protected by Google's synced passkey implementation. The research reveals vulnerabilities in passkey synchronization that could undermine the authentication security model that passkeys are designed to provide.

top_stories.title: Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication
top_stories.summary: A security analysis identifies an attack surface in passkey (passwordless authentication) implementations where relying parties fail to validate the User Verified (UV) flag. This implementation gap can reduce what is intended as multi-factor authentication down to a single factor, undermining the security guarantees of passkey-based systems.

top_stories.title: Snowflake hacker pleads guilty, faces up to 32 years in prison
top_stories.summary: Connor Riley Moucka, a Canadian man known as "Waifu" and "Judische," pleaded guilty in federal court to hacking customer accounts at cloud storage provider Snowflake and stealing data from over 165 organizations. He faces up to 32 years in prison on charges including computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and conspiracy, with sentencing scheduled for October 27.

top_stories.title: Microsoft extends zero trust deeper into enterprise AI
top_stories.summary: Microsoft updated its Zero Trust Assessment tool and Zero Trust Workshop as part of its Zero Trust for AI strategy. The updates add an AI pillar to the Zero Trust Assessment tool and extend zero trust principles to AI agents and AI-assisted software development environments.

top_stories.title: Kali365 Weaponizes Microsoft Authentication Against US Companies: New Enterprise Risk
top_stories.summary: A phishing kit called Kali365 is exploiting Microsoft's device code authentication flow to gain unauthorized access to corporate resources at US organizations. Attackers use attacker-controlled device codes that victims approve on legitimate Microsoft authentication pages, after which the resulting access and refresh tokens grant persistent access to email, documents, and cloud resources.

news.title: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
news.summary: Swiss federal IT office confirmed hackers exploited vulnerabilities in its Microsoft SharePoint servers, compromising approximately 200 accounts. The breach involved government infrastructure and resulted in unauthorized access to a significant number of user accounts.

news.title: Discounted Claude access bought on the gray market may expose every prompt you send
news.summary: Okta discovered more than half a dozen services on underground forums offering discounted or "unlimited" access to frontier AI models like Claude, which they believe are largely driven by Chinese users circumventing regulatory and provider restrictions. The services raise security concerns as users' prompts may be exposed when routing through unauthorized intermediary access points.

news.title: Snowflake Hacker Pleads Guilty Over Breaches Affecting at Least 100 Million People
news.summary: Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty in Seattle federal court to computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and conspiracy related to the 2024 Snowflake customer account breaches. The intrusions compromised at least 165 organizations, exposed records of over 100 million people, and netted Moucka at least $495,000.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved credential-based unauthorized access to Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in data theft including over 100 million AT&T customer records.

news.title: Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server Reaches General Availability
news.summary: Microsoft has launched the Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server into general availability, providing a hosted solution for AI assistant access to Azure DevOps projects. The server eliminates local setup requirements for connecting AI tools to Azure DevOps resources.

news.title: How AI-powered phishing killed blocklists for good
news.summary: Push Security argues that AI-powered phishing attacks generate disposable infrastructure and rapidly evolving toolkits that render traditional blocklist-based defenses obsolete. The company advocates for browser-level, technique-based detection as a more effective alternative to domain and signature-based indicators for defending against credential phishing.

news.title: Leaked n8n API Tokens Exposed Live Instances to Credential Theft
news.summary: GitGuardian researchers discovered 4,576 unique n8n API tokens exposed in public GitHub commits, linked to 1,255 hostnames, with 321 live instances accepting the leaked credentials. Researchers demonstrated four attack methods using these tokens to access sensitive data and downstream credentials without requiring any software vulnerability exploitation.

news.title: From 2 weeks to 2 minutes: Amazon Cognito launches Provisioned limits for self-service rate limit management
news.summary: Amazon Cognito has launched a "Provisioned limits" feature that enables self-service rate limit management, reducing the time to adjust limits from two weeks to two minutes. The feature targets teams managing customer identity workloads who need to handle elevated traffic for application activities without waiting for manual AWS support intervention.

news.title: When Hackers and AI Agents Share the Same Trick: The Trust Paradox Behind the Brinks Home Breach
news.summary: The Brinks Home breach involved social engineering where an attacker called an IT administrator and manipulated them into granting unauthorized access, exploiting human trust in authentication processes. The article uses this incident to examine how AI agents and human attackers exploit the same trust mechanisms in identity verification and access authorization workflows.

news.title: Catching rogue AI behavior with identity-aware analytics
news.summary: An identity-aware AI Gateway has entered open beta, combining identity context with AI traffic analysis to establish behavioral baselines for users and agents. The product flags insider risk by correlating AI activity with identity data, applying behavioral analytics to both human and non-human identities.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with vishing attacks doubling, according to new research. These social engineering techniques bypass entrenched authentication security controls by exploiting the OAuth device authorization flow, which is directly relevant to MFA and identity-based attack vectors.

news.title: Greatness PhaaS Adds Device Code Phishing to Bypass MFA and Steal Tokens
news.summary: The Greatness phishing-as-a-service toolkit has added device code phishing capabilities that abuse the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant flow to bypass MFA and steal authentication tokens. The attack technique uses adversary-in-the-middle methods to capture credentials and session tokens, effectively circumventing MFA protections.

news.title: Keyv-Linked npm Worm Poisons Hundreds of Packages, Plants Claude Code and VS Code Hooks
news.summary: A credential-stealing npm worm originating in keyv@6.0.0 spread to hundreds of packages across the npm registry on August 4, 2026. SafeDep verified 353 poisoned versions across 79 package names, with broader estimates reaching 868 affected packages according to Aikido.

news.title: Watch out — Microsoft login pages are being abused as hackers try and lure in unlucky victims, here's what to look out for
news.summary: Hackers are abusing Microsoft login pages to gain unauthorized access to organizational accounts across approximately 120 organizations. The attack bypassed traditional credential theft and MFA by exploiting OAuth or token-based mechanisms, compromising mail, files, Teams, SharePoint, and calendars.

news.title: Edit on-prem Exchange attributes in Exchange Online with writeback for cloud-managed remote mailboxes
news.summary: Microsoft has made Exchange attribute writeback for cloud-managed remote mailboxes generally available. The feature allows management of Exchange mailbox attributes in Exchange Online while syncing a limited set of values back to on-premises Active Directory.

news.title: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
news.summary: Microsoft has expanded its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance targeting security for AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The release addresses how Zero Trust principles apply to emerging AI agent architectures and development security operations pipelines.

news.title: Entra Connect gets a 2026 cutoff as Microsoft urges Tier 0 treatment
news.summary: Microsoft has set a September 30, 2026 deadline for Entra Connect administrators to upgrade to version 2.5.79.0 or later, after which synchronization will stop on older versions. Microsoft is also directing organizations to treat Entra Connect as a Tier 0 asset, reflecting its privileged role in hybrid identity infrastructure.

news.title: Obsidian Security raises $85M as AI agents create cybersecurity’s next major attack surface
news.summary: Obsidian Security raised an $85 million Series D funding round, reaching a post-money valuation of $1.1 billion. The company focuses on securing access by autonomous AI agents to cloud applications, positioning itself in the identity and access security space.

news.title: ServiceNow gives Autonomous Security AI Specialists to close exposures faster
news.summary: ServiceNow is expanding its Autonomous Security framework with AI Specialists designed to investigate and remediate security issues with limited human intervention. The framework unifies six security areas including identity governance and vulnerability management.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem on a data breach in which a contractor accidentally published dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, to a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management failures and exposure risks relevant to IAM and secrets management practices.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two Scattered Spider members pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise large organizations.
